title: Slim down runtime dependencies and rewrite continuous-batcher signalling to reduce tail latency
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Our continuous-batcher path shows recurring tail-latency spikes under mixed short/long-sequence workloads. Investigation points at two correlated sources: (1) bloated runtime dependency graph (several crates and third-party libs pinned to older semver with conservative feature sets) causing excess allocations and cold-path heap churn, and (2) noisy signalling between the batcher and the KV cache adapter which triggers synchronous cache refills and scheduler wakeups. These lead to 95th/99th percentile latency regressions and increased token cost due to misaligned batching windows.

Scope & Goal: Reduce 99th percentile token latency by at least 25% on mixed workloads and lower resident set size under steady-state by ~15% by: (A) slimming dependencies (remove unused features, upgrade to lightweight async primitives, eliminate duplicate allocators), (B) replacing synchronous KV refill triggers with an async, debounce-based signalling layer in the batcher, and (C) adding targeted telemetry to validate behaviour. This ticket bundles the refactor and the deps work as a single deliverable due to strong coupling at the interface.

Approach:
1) Dependency audit & slimdown (spike + PRs): generate crate feature matrix for runtime crates; remove unused features and duplicated allocators; upgrade tokio->1.27 (selective), replace heavy serde_json parsing on hot-paths with a small fast-deser shim; defer optional telemetry sinks behind feature flags.
2) New signalling contract: introduce an async backoff/debounce signal (BatchSignal v2) between batcher and KV adapter that batches wakeups on a low-latency timer and exposes a non-blocking try_wake path for high-priority short sequences.
3) Implement small arena-based temporary allocator for tokenization hot-path to avoid transient heap allocations.
4) Observability: add span-level traces for signal generation, queue length histograms binned by sequence length, and a cache-refill counter with latency buckets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Performance: 99th percentile token latency down by >=25% on the mixed benchmark harness (see attachments).
- Memory: resident set size reduced by >=15% for steady-state 500 concurrent short sessions run.
- Tests: unit tests for BatchSignal semantics + integration tests exercising KV refill paths under synthetic load.
- Rollout: canary deploy with 10% traffic and automated rollback on SLO violations.

Notes: This is a refactor-heavy change; the design doc details the new vector-based signal queue to avoid mutex contention and the debounce heuristics for prefetch windows.
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed - feature-matrix spreadsheet uploaded. Observed two crates contributing ~12% of extra allocations (json/tokenizer helper, legacy allocator).
2026-03-04: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/BatchSignal-v2-and-deps-slimdown (internal) - design reviewed by runtime and infra leads (Maya, Tomas).

2026-03-06: Prototype of BatchSignal v2 implemented in feature branch eng/ENG-258421/signal-prototype. Preliminary microbench shows 18% reduction in wakeup-count under mixed load. PR: https://github.com/redwood/re inference/pull/4312
2026-03-09: Dependency PRs prepared - tokio upgraded in runtime-core with feature flags toggled. Removing serde_json from hot path replaced by fast-shim parser (benchmarks attached).
2026-03-10: Integration test added for concurrent refill races; flaky edge surfaced where a fast retry path bypassed debounce. Added fix to priority fast-path to ensure try_wake remains lock-free.
comments: Jonah Li (2026-03-03): We should validate the arena allocator against our NUMA machines. If fragmentation improves on linux-x86 but regresses on ppc64, we need a fallthrough. Added as TODO.
Maya Chen (runtime lead, 2026-03-05): Good trade-off. Keep the fast-path non-blocking; prefer a small extra memory overhead over added mutexes. Approve prototype approach.
PM: Elliott Vargas (2026-03-07): Customer customers running PLG workloads have seen tail jitter. Please flag any user-facing degradation during canary early. Prioritize rollback hooks.
risk: Medium. Main risk is behavioral regressions from changing allocator semantics on edge workloads and inadvertently delaying high-priority short-sequence wakeups. Mitigations: keep feature-flagged rollout, extensive integration tests, NUMA-targeted perf runs, and automatic rollback thresholds in canary stage.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind runtime-1.22 feature flag. 2) Internal staging run with 200 concurrent sessions for 24h. 3) Canary 10% in production for 48h with SLO gates: 99p latency increase < 5ms and cache-refill error rate < 0.1%. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% over 72h if stable. 5) Emergency rollback script prepared and tested.
